binding.note: Every entry is a digest a run wrote about itself. The watcher groups record one digest per process in samples[].summary.exe_sha256, so w1 and w2 are bound by what their own processes reported rather than by inference from a neighbouring group. No binary is archived: a rebuild replaces the file in place and MSVC links are not byte-reproducible, so the reproducible artifact is the instrumented source in git plus these digests.

findings.what: the probe on disk is not the probe the groups measured
findings.subject: cuexis_execution_device_probe.exe
findings.note: the probe links cuexis_json_support and the engine, so the direct writer and the chart trace scopes relinked it without a probe source change; the w1 probe is a third digest again, and its prepare-trace vocabulary is identical to the group probe's, so the watcher numbers stay comparable in form while every number in this table still belongs to the digest that produced it. Attribute nothing to the binary now on disk without a fresh group

findings.what: trace perturbation measured on the superseded group
findings.subject: 20261101-a
findings.note: armed in blocks, so the order effect is inside this number; it is the reason the authoritative group alternates arms

findings.what: device-handshake probe stages are wider than the 15 % limit
findings.subject: 2 millisecond-scale stages that no claim uses
findings.note: backend_create, first_extract, first_submit and the neighbouring handshake stages move by milliseconds between fresh processes while their median is tens of milliseconds. They are reported as medians only; the comparative numbers in this table are the first frame total and playback_prepare, which are inside the limit.

findings.what: the traced prepare split inside the startup probe groups is too noisy to compare
findings.subject: 3 trace stages over the limit

detail.note: these groups exist to show the shape of the split and to bound the trace perturbation; the split numbers quoted in the report come from the dedicated serializer group, which is gated separately and passes

findings.note: a startup probe process also creates the device and reads pixels, so a 20 % excursion on chart_typed_read is possible there. Rather than widen the limit, the split comparison was re-run as its own N=3 group over the canonical sweep, where every quoted stage is inside 15 %.

findings.what: sub-millisecond probe stages cannot meet a 15 % relative limit
findings.subject: 92 quantities whose median is under 1000 us
findings.note: gl_context, pixel_readback, backend_activate and the other device-handshake stages are microseconds wide, so 15 % of them is far below the clock and driver jitter floor; they are reported with their medians and never used as a claim.

findings.what: the superseded group violates the repeatability limit
findings.subject: spread_pct > 15 on measured stages
findings.note: this is the confound the interleaved group removes, recorded rather than hidden

findings.subject: counts, not durations
findings.note: a count varies with how many probes fit after the window appears; the latency distribution is the responsiveness measure, not the count

findings.what: 20261101-w2 player-40k-untraced-close1 records a close latency for a close that had no window to land on
findings.subject: 1 process(es)

detail.note: watch_window.py posts WM_CLOSE to the window it currently believes is primary and stamps wm_close_to_exit_s regardless of whether the post happened, so for this arm that field is the remainder of the watcher's timeout, not a close latency

findings.note: the close deadline falls before the primary window exists, so PostMessageW is never called; the number is correct as an artefact and is excluded from every shutdown claim. The device-first arm is the valid counterpart, because there a window exists at the same 1 s deadline.

findings.what: the device-first window is visible but does not pump messages while preparing
findings.subject: probe timeouts inside the prepare window
findings.note: the user can see the window and can post WM_CLOSE, but the close is only serviced once prepare returns; this is why the order is a perceived latency improvement and not a responsiveness fix

notes: runs/20261101-w1 and runs/20261101-w2 persisted every child's stdout and stderr under raw/ and every process's own summary inside watch-set.json samples[], so the executable digest, the command line, the environment overrides and the start time are recorded per process without needing --json on watch_window.py. What the aggregate file does not keep is a standalone per-process JSON document; the next watcher group should still pass --json so that each process has a file of its own whose digest can be checked independently.

20261101-a and 20261101-a2 measured the same question with different orders. a2 is the authoritative perturbation group; a is kept because it is what a batched order produces, and dropping it would hide that ordering effect.

runs/smoke-w2/smoke-wf-01 exited 0xC0000409 (3221226505): the first window-first patch moved a device call off the owner thread and the process died. smoke-wf2-01 is the fix. Both are kept as the record of why the shipped order is thread-free.
The 40000 entity arms are a stress case chosen to expose the prepare path, not a quality gate; the 2000 ms first-frame clamp is cited only to state the distance.
